pain_points: Calls are missed on busy weekend mornings when the tee sheet is packed and there is a line in the pro shop, forcing staff to choose between the people in the shop and the caller
After 6:00 the pro shop line forwards to the restaurant and unanswered calls ring at the bar after about six rings, so after-hours booking calls are handled by whoever is at the bar
No visibility into after-hours call volume - Sam could not give numbers, only that they get quite a few
current_solution: Phone tree with options for the pro shop and the restaurant; the pro shop line forwards automatically to the restaurant at 6:00, and an unanswered pro shop line rings at the bar after about six rings. Club Caddy holds the tee sheet, applying member rates automatically from purchased passes, with bookings taken 14 days out for members and public alike.
features_demoed: Live AI voice concierge call placed to Tradition Golf Club (the demo target, not the prospect)
Returning-caller recognition and greeting by name
Tee-time search for a foursome with alternative times offered and a total price quoted
Read-back and confirmation of the booking, with text confirmation and pay-at-the-pro-shop
Weather guarantee link offered in the confirmation text
Practice facility answer, with lesson pricing deferred to a pro shop transfer
Dashboard call list with recording and full transcript of every call
Built-in waitlist with a text notification and a 10-minute window to confirm
Notice board for daily items such as cart path only, woven into the conversation by the AI
Delayed call forwarding configuration and an on/off toggle in the dashboard
prospect_questions: Their tee sheet requires an email address to hold a customer in the database - can the system capture that through a phone call?
unanswered_questions: Whether the voice agent collects an email address on the call for a first-time booker. Sam noted Club Caddy asks for first name, last name, email and phone number; the answer given was that CourseRev keys on the phone number, stores the email, and prompts new players for the information the course collects, without confirming email capture on the call.

objections.trigger_quote: Uh yeah, because obviously this is something that I got to run through the owners at our board meeting.
objections.rep_response_summary: Jason agreed immediately, offered to produce high-level owner notes from the call recording covering what owners care about and how the system works with the pro shop, restated that there is no operational disruption because it runs as a call forward the course can toggle on and off, and proposed following up at the end of the following week. He also offered to send the standard terms and the onboarding form for review in the meantime.

open.evidence: Cordial but flat and unprepared - he had not looked into CourseRev before the call and answered the operations questions in one- and two-word replies, opening up only on the missed-call problem: "we probably miss more in the morning than we do, especially weekend mornings when it's t-shirts packed and there's a line out the door in the pro shop".

post_demo.evidence: Reaction to the live booking demo and the dashboard walkthrough was limited to short acknowledgements - "Yep.", "Sure.", "Okay." - with no questions asked; when invited to ask questions just before the demo his answer was "Uh, not" "yet."

at_pricing.evidence: The $2.50-per-round-played model, with no charge for no-shows or cancellations, drew "Okay." and "Sure." and no questions about cost at any point in the call.

close.evidence: Volunteered the internal route himself and committed to it - "we meet every Wednesday" - then accepted the plan to receive the terms, onboarding form and owner notes: "If you want to do that and then I'll till Wednesday and then we can go from" there.
